Organocatalytic enantioselective [2 + 4]-
annulation of γ-substituted allenoates with
N-acyldiazenes for the synthesis of optically
active 1,3,4-oxadiazines†
Xing Guo,a,b Xuling Chen,a Yuyu Cheng,a Xiaoyong Chang,a Xuechen Li
 *b and
Pengfei Li
 *a
An enantioselective [2 + 4]-annulation of γ-substituted allenoates
with N-acyldiazenes has been developed for the ﬁrst time. In the
presence of an L-proline-derived DMAP analogue, the annulation
proceeded smoothly to a ﬀord a broad range of 1,3,4-oxadiazine
derivatives in good to excellent yields with high stereoselectivities.
1,3,4-Oxadiazine is a class of core structural units widely occur-
ring in a number of bioactive molecules, which exhibit diversi-
fied bioactivities (Scheme 1A). 1 Accordingly, the e ﬃcient syn-
thesis of these heterocycles featuring 1,3,4-oxadiazine has
therefore attracted intensive interest. 2 In terms of organo-
catalysis, Wang and Meng et al. reported a 4-dimethyl-
aminopyridine (DMAP)-catalyzed [2 + 4]-cycloaddition between
allenoates3 and N-acyldiazenes4 for the synthesis of racemic
1,3,4-oxadiazine derivatives (Scheme 1B). 5 It was proposed that
the cycloaddition is triggered by the S N2 attack of nucleophilic
DMAP on the allenoate to give a zwitterionic intermediate, fol-
lowed by γ-addition of N-acyldiazene, intramolecular Michael
addition of an oxygen anion, and elimination of DMAP to
regenerate the catalyst and a ﬀord the desired product. The
density functional theory calculation indicated that the
addition of DMAP to γ-methyl allenoate is the rate-determining
step, and the reaction of chiral γ-methyl allenoate and
N-acyldiazene is both the regio- and enantioselective-determin-
ing step.
6 It should be noted that many organocatalytic asym-
metric reactions of γ-substituted allenoates 7 and
N-acyldiazenes8 have been established previously, but the orga-
nocatalytic stereoselective [2 + 4]-annulation of racemic
γ-substituted allenoates and N-acyldiazenes has not been rea-
lized yet. The development of an organocatalytic asymmetric
synthesis strategy for optically active 1,3,4-oxadiazines is there-
fore highly desirable.
As nucleophilic catalysts, enantioenriched structurally
diverse DMAP analogues have been particularly attractive
targets in the field of asymmetric organocatalysis.
9 For
examples, L-proline-derived DMAP analogues have been suc-
cessfully employed as e ﬃcient catalysts in the asymmetric
kinetic resolution of sec-alcohols,10 and [3 + 2]-annulation of
MBH carbonates. 11 In consideration of a similar activation
mechanism with MBH carbonate, allenoates were expected to
be activated by
L-proline-derived DMAP analogues to generate
the desired enantioenriched products. Based on our previous
works on organocatalytic asymmetric annulations of MBH car-
bonates,

istry of allene, 13 herein we report an L-proline-derived DMAP
analogue catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation between γ-substituted
allenoates and N-acyldiazenes towards optically active 1,3,4-
oxadiazine derivatives (Scheme 1C).
To address the enantioselectivity issue, the annulation of
racemic γ-benzyl allenoate 1a with N-phenyl-N′-benzoyldiazene
2aa was investigated as a model reaction (Table 1). Inspired by
Wang and Meng ’ work, we initially focused on the catalyst
screening of chiral DMAP analogues. In the presence of cata-
lyst C1 derived from quinine, a trace of the desired product
3aaa was obtained (Table 1, entry 1). An essential enhance-
ment was achieved when the
L-proline-derived DMAP analogue
C2 was employed as the catalyst, a ﬀording the desired product
3aaa in 32% yield with 29% ee (Table 1, entry 2). A further
survey on L-proline-derived DMAP analogues indicated that all
probed catalysts could prompt the reaction to a ﬀord the
desired 1,3,4-oxadiazine 3aaa with fluctuating enantioselectivi-
ties and yields (Table 1, entries 1 –6). In particular, catalyst C5
enabled the formation of the desired product 3aaa in 32%
yield with 75% ee (Table 1, entry 5). To obtain a satisfactory
yield and stereoselectivity, further optimization of reaction
conditions was then carried out in the presence of catalyst C5.
The screening of reaction media indicated that the solvent had
a significant impact on the yield and a slight e ﬀect on the
enantioselectivity (Table 1, entries 7 –14). Notably, the yield
was improved to 67% without compromising the ee value
when the C5 catalyzed reaction was carried out in methyl
t-butyl ether (MTBE, Table 1, entry 14). It was found that both
yield and ee were sensitive to the concentration (Table 1,
entries 15 –17), and 1.5 mL MTBE was identified to be more
suitable to a ﬀord product 3aaa in 65% yield with 75% ee. No
further improvement in terms of enantioselectivity and yield
was obtained after the evaluation of the reactant ratio (Table 1,
entries 18 –20). Pleasingly, the desired 1,3,4-oxadiazine 3aaa
could be obtained in 70% yield with 74% ee when the reaction
was carried out at 30 °C (Table 1, entry 21). Further modifying
the catalyst loading and reaction time revealed that product
3aaa could be formed in 82% yield with 71% ee (Table 1,
entries 23 –25). As a result, the optimal reaction conditions
were identified as follows: N-phenyl-N′-benzoyldiazene 2aa
(0.3 mmol) was added to a solution of racemic γ-benzyl alleno-
ate 1a (0.2 mmol) with C5 (15 mol%) in MTBE (1.5 mL) at
30 °C and reacted for 48 h; the desired 1,3,4-oxadiazine 3aaa
was obtained in 82% with 71% ee.
Having identified the optimal conditions, we sought to
explore the scope of the C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation
between γ-substituted allenoates 1 and N-acyldiazenes 2.A s
shown in Table 2, we first examined the scope of
N-acyldiazenes 2 by the C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation of
racemic γ-benzyl allenoate 1a. Generally, these reactions pro-
ceeded smoothly to a ﬀord the corresponding 1,3,4-oxadiazines
3
with good yields and enantioselectivity. Importantly, various
substituents, including electron-withdrawing (F, Cl, Br) and
electron-donating (Me) groups, could be introduced to the
para-position of the aromatic ring of Ar 2 with only minor
eﬀects on the yields and asymmetric induction (Table 2,
entries 1 –5). Notably, the C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation of
2-methyl-N-( phenylimino)benzamide 2af also a ﬀorded the
desired 1,3,4-oxadiazine 3aaf in 88% yield with 71% ee
(Table 2, entry 6). Accordingly, the reactions of the bulk
N-acyldiazenes 2 were investigated. 1-Naphthyl (Ar 2) was found
to be tolerated, furnishing the product 3aag in 77% yield with
70% ee (Table 2, entry 7). Using N-acyldiazene 2ah (Ar2 = 3,4-
dimethoxylphenyl) enabled the formation of the product 3aah
in 71% yield with 74% ee (Table 2, entry 8). Similar results
were obtained from the reaction of N-acyldiazene 2ai (Ar2 =
3,5-dimethoxylphenyl, Table 2, entry 9). In particular, 1,3,4-
oxadiazine 3aaj was obtained in 77% yield with 78% ee from
the C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation of N-acyldiazene 2aj (Ar
2 =
3,4,5-trimethoxylphenyl, Table 2, entry 10). The sterically
encumbered N-acyldiazene 2ak (Ar
2 = 1-adamantyl) was also
compatible to furnish the corresponding product 3aak in 87%

yield with 75% ee (Table 2, entry 11). With these encouraging
results in hand, the e ﬀect of the aromatic residue Ar 1 on the
C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation was then examined. Pleasingly,
both electron-withdrawing (F, Cl, Br, I, CF 3) and electron-
donating (Me, i-Pr, t-Bu, BnO) groups on the aromatic ring of
Ar1 were accommodated under the standard conditions to
furnish products 3abj–asj in 72 –93% yields with 72 –80% ee
(Table 2, entries 12 –29). Furthermore, the reaction of
N-acyldiazene 2tj (Ar1 = 2-naphthyl, Ar 2 = 3,4,5-trimethoxylphe-
nyl) generated the corresponding product 3atj in 76% yield
with 87% ee (Table 2, entry 30). In addition, the heteroaro-
matic N-acyldiazene 2uj (Ar1 = 2-pyridinyl) also reacted
smoothly with γ-benzyl allenoate 1a to aﬀord the product 3auj
in 74% yield with 82% ee (Table 2, entry 31). Taken altogether,
the C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation of γ-benzyl allenoate 1a was
successfully extended to a broad scope of N-acyldiazenes, fur-
nishing the desired 1,3,4-oxadiazine derivatives in good to
excellent yields with high stereoselectivities.
To further explore the scope and limitations of the reaction,
the scope of γ-substituted allenoates 1 was then examined by
the C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation of N-acyldiazene 2tj
(Table 3). Under the standard conditions, γ-ethyl allenoate 1b
reacted smoothly with N-acyldiazene 2tj,a ﬀording the corres-
ponding product 3btj in 76% yield with 75% ee (Table 3, entry
1). The reaction of γ-propyl allenoate 1c enabled the formation
of product 3ctj in 73% yield with 82% ee (Table 3, entry 2).
The ester group (CO 2R2) of allenoates 1 was found to a ﬀect the
reaction slightly, furnishing 1,3,4-oxadiazines 3dtj–ftj in
72–82% yield with 74 –81% ee (Table 3, entries 3 –5). In all, an
organocatalytic enantioselective [2 + 4]-annulation of racemic
γ-substituted allenoates and N-acyldiazenes has been estab-
lished, which featured mild conditions, wide substrate scope,
high e ﬃciency and stereoselectivity. Importantly, this method
provided a direct way to optically activate 1,3,4-oxadiazines.
With these encouraging results in hand, we then tried to
determine the absolute configuration of products 3 by X-ray
crystallography. Interestingly, the crystal of product 3aac was
found to contain a pair of enantiomers ( R)-3aac and ( S)-
3aac.14a The ee value of the residual product 3aac in the
mother solution turned to be 99%. Furthermore, the crystal of
product 3aak was also comprised of racemic 3aak.
14b
To illustrate the synthetic potential of this reaction, a scale-
up experiment was carried out under the optimal reaction con-
ditions. The C5-catalyzed [2 + 4]-annulation between 1.5 mmol
of racemic γ-benzyl allenoate 1a and 1.0 mmol of
N-acyldiazene 2tj proceeded smoothly to furnish the desired
1,3,4-oxadiazine 3atj in 76% yield with 87% ee (Scheme 2A).
Upon treatment with Br
2/Et3N in dichloromethane at room
temperature, bromination of the product 3aaa proceeded
smoothly to furnish the corresponding product 4aaa in 62%
yield with 76% ee (Scheme 2B). Reduction of the ester group
aﬀorded alcohol 5aaa in 88% yield without compromising the
enantioselectivity. Further esterification of chiral alcohol 5aaa
generated products 6aaa in 78% yield with 76% ee and 7aaa in
68% yield with 76% ee, respectively.

probable reaction mechanism was proposed in Scheme 3. An

initial addition of nucleophilic L-proline-derived DMAP ana-
logue C5 on the racemic γ-benzyl allenoate 1a delivered the
intermediate IM-1. Then the conjugate addition of IM-1 to
N-acyldiazene 2aa furnished the intermediate IM-2, followed
by an intramolecular 1,4-addition to a ﬀord the intermediate
IM-3. Finally, the elimination reaction led to the formation of
the desired product 3aaa and regeneration of the chiral catalyst
C5. Obviously, both the regio- and enantioselectivity originated
from the reaction of the chiral intermediate IM-1 with
N-acyldiazene 2aa.
In conclusion, we have successfully developed an e ﬃcient
organocatalytic asymmetric [2 + 4] annulation of γ-substituted
allenoates with N-acyldiazenes. In the presence of an L-proline-
derived DMAP analogue, the reaction proceeds well to furnish
a broad range of chiral 1,3,4-oxadiazines with high yields and
stereoselectivities.
